name: ratio-bars
title: Ratio bars
tagline: Ratio as equal-unit part-bars at simplified and actual scales joined by ×k/÷k arrows; derives the share value and every quantity from one known.
description: A ratio a : b (: c) shown as adjacent equal-unit part-bars at two scales — the simplified ratio on top and the actual quantities beneath — joined by ×k / ÷k scale-factor arrows, where k is the value of one share. You write the ratio (`parts`, each with its `units` number) and exactly one known quantity (`known`: a total, one part, or the difference between two parts); the model derives the simplest form (÷ HCF), the scale factor k, every part's quantity, the total, and each part's fraction of the whole. Parts and quantities occlude to "?" for questions and highlight in amber; `occludeSimplified` poses "write this in its simplest form". An optional `combineWith` ratio that shares a named term draws the combine figure: both ratios scaled to the common term (LCM) and merged into one bar, the shared term aligned and ambered. Covers simplifying, scaling up/down, sharing a total, finding a quantity from a total / a part / a difference, the unit value, ratio ↔ fraction, and combining two ratios.
whenToUse: Reach for this whenever a ratio is taught through the ×k / ÷k relationship between its simplest form and the actual amounts: simplifying (18 : 12 → 3 : 2 by dividing by the HCF), scaling up or down (2 : 3 = 8 : 12), sharing a total in a ratio (£56 in 5 : 3 → £35 : £21), finding one quantity from a given total, from one known part, or from the difference between two parts ("A : B = 7 : 4 and A is 24 more than B"), the unit value (what one share is worth), ratio ↔ fraction (each part as a fraction of the whole — 5 : 3 means 5/8 and 3/8), and combining two ratios that share a term. Author the semantics: list the `parts` with their `units` (the ratio numbers — you may write them un-simplified), then give exactly one `known` — `{ type: "total", value }`, `{ type: "part", part, value }`, or `{ type: "difference", between: [i, j], value }`. You never write a quantity, a unit value, or a width; the model computes them all. To pose a question: `occlude` a part to hide its quantity ("find this share" — the scale factor and the total are hidden too so they can't give it away), set `show.values: false` (and, for a fully blank space, `show.unitValue: false`) for an answer space with the quantities left to fill, set `occludeSimplified: true` to ask for the simplest form, or set `show.unitValue: false` to ask for the scale factor. `highlight` a part to mark the answer; add `unit` ("£", or "ml" with `after: true`) so quantities read as money or measures; set `show.fractions: true` to label each part with its fraction of the whole. Combine: give `combineWith` a second ratio whose `parts` reuse exactly one `name` from the primary (A:B = 2:3 plus B:C = 4:5, sharing "B"); the model finds the common term (LCM), scales each ratio to it, and draws the merged ratio with the shared part aligned — leave `known` out, it does not apply to combine. Cross-block convention: keep the same parts, names and `unit` across a lesson so pupils track one diagram; change only what is shaded, occluded or asked. A staged build reads well — open on the simplified ratio, bring in the arrows and the unit value, then the quantities last. Switch model when the teaching is not the ratio scale relationship: for a generic part–whole or comparison strip, a fraction of an amount, a percentage bar or an equation bar model use number/bar-model; for fraction equivalence/comparison use number/fraction-wall. Synonyms a teacher might use: ratio, simplify a ratio, simplest form, equivalent ratios, share in a ratio, scale factor, unit value, one part, parts, ratio table, divide in a given ratio, combine ratios, ratio to fraction.

part.description: One part of the ratio, left to right. Its ratio number is `units`; everything shown for it (its simplified number, its actual quantity, its fraction of the whole) is derived. Add `name`, or `occlude`/`highlight` to pose or emphasise.

units.description: The ratio number for this part — its count of equal shares. For the ratio 5 : 3 the parts are units 5 and 3; for 2 : 3 : 5 they are 2, 3, 5. Whole numbers only; the ratio need NOT be in its simplest form (write 18 : 12 as units 18 and 12 — the model simplifies it). Each part is drawn as this many equal unit squares.

name.description: A name for this part, centred above its run — "Sand", "Boys", "A". Omit for an unnamed part. Keep names short; they sit over the bar.

occlude.description: Render THIS part's actual quantity as "?" — the "find this share" hook. The part stays visible and correctly sized; the simplified number and any total still show. Default false.

highlight.description: Draw this part in amber instead of its categorical colour — the share in focus or the answer. Use sparingly (amber is the result colour). Default false.

parts.description: The ratio, left to right — two to five parts, each with its `units` (ratio number). Write the ratio as it appears in the problem; if it is not in simplest form (e.g. 18 : 12) the model derives the simplified row from it.

known.description: The ONE given quantity that scales the actual-quantity row. Omit it to show the ratio at its authored scale (the simplify / equivalent-ratio case: the actual row shows your numbers, the top row their simplest form). Give at most one known.

type.description: "total": `value` is the total of ALL the quantities (share a total). "part": `value` is the quantity of the single part named by `part` (find the rest from one). "difference": `value` is the gap between the two parts named by `between` (find the rest from a difference).

value.description: The amount of the known: the total, the one part, or the difference — depending on `type`.

part.description: Required when `type` is "part": which part the `value` belongs to, counted from 1 at the left.

between.description: Required when `type` is "difference": the two parts (1-based, left to right) whose quantities differ by `value`, e.g. [1, 2] for "the first is `value` more than the second".

unit.description: A currency or measure symbol applied to every actual quantity. Omit for bare numbers.

after.description: Place the symbol AFTER the number with a space ("350 ml") instead of before it ("£24"). Default false (before, no space).

combineWith.description: A SECOND ratio to combine with `parts` through a shared term — the LCM-combine figure. Its `parts` must reuse exactly ONE `name` from the primary ratio (the shared term, e.g. both ratios name a part "B"). The model finds the common value of the shared term (the LCM of its two `units`), scales each ratio to it, and draws the merged ratio with the shared part aligned and ambered. `known` does not apply when combining — omit it.

parts.description: The second ratio's parts. Exactly one must share a `name` with a part of the primary ratio; the others are new parts of the combined ratio.

occludeSimplified.description: Render the simplified-ratio row's numbers as "?" — the "write this ratio in its simplest form" hook. The unit squares are suppressed so their count cannot leak the answer; the actual quantities (your authored ratio) stay visible. Default false.

values.description: Show every derived actual quantity. Default true. Set false for an answer space — all quantities are left blank for pupils to fill, while the simplified ratio and any GIVEN total still show. For a fully blank answer space also set `unitValue: false` (otherwise the scale factor on the arrows hands pupils the answer in one step); leave `unitValue: true` to give the scale factor as a hint.

unitValue.description: Show the scale factor k (the value of one share) on the ×k / ÷k arrows. Default true. Set false to pose "what is the scale factor?" — the arrows then read "× ?" / "÷ ?".

arrows.description: Show the ×k (down, left) and ÷k (up, right) scale-factor arrows between the two rows. Default true. Only drawn when the two rows differ (k ≠ 1).

unitSquares.description: Subdivide each part into its count of equal unit squares (the "equal-unit" look). Default true. Automatically suppressed when the simplified parts total more than 20 squares, or when `occludeSimplified` is set; the parts then draw as solid boxes.

fractions.description: Label each part with its fraction of the whole (5 : 3 → 5/8 and 3/8) — the ratio ↔ fraction reading. Default false.

total.description: Brace the actual-quantity row with its total — drawn only when a `known` quantity is given (the total is meaningless without one). Default true. A GIVEN total (a "total" known) always shows; a DERIVED total reads "?" whenever a part is occluded or `show.values` is false, so it can never leak a hidden share.

header.description: Optional short title centred above the figure; the top padding grows to clear it.

caption.description: Optional line centred below the figure, e.g. a short context note. Never the question or an instruction: that wording is the block's text.
